target_customer: Consumers tracking fitness and body composition (preorder $500 in 2017), later businesses such as gyms and medspas
problem: Whole-body scanners existed for about 15 years but were large and expensive, and regular scales do not show where fat is lost and muscle gained.
business_model: Hardware sales of a 3D body scanner scale plus later B2B offering and software; consumer preorders in 2017
product_category: Consumer and business 3D body scanner hardware

founders.name: Alexandre Wayenberg
founders.background_notes: YC page and VentureBeat name him as CEO; no background found in opened sources.

founders.name: Martin Kessler
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he is into D2C, growth marketing, recruiting, hardware and fitness. Education not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building an accurate, affordable 3D body scanner with depth sensing, body composition estimation and consumer hardware manufacturing was hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware and computer vision know-how and design are hard to copy quickly, but several scanning rivals existed and patents were not found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; rivals later marketed lower cost software-based scanning, and the company stayed independent.

market_need_then: VentureBeat (May 2017) reports preorders reaching six figures in dollars and a waitlist of about 75,000 followers for a $500 scanner, evidence of consumer interest in 3D body tracking.

branding.domain_note: Uses shapescale.com; company legal name is Shape and product name ShapeScale, domain history not found.

identity.visual_style: Consumer hardware product design; a Red Dot project page exists per search results (not opened)
identity.voice_and_tone: Health and fitness goal language such as transforming how we measure health goals

branding.brand_signature: The 3D avatar shown on the scale display
branding.community_and_virality: A waitlist of about 75,000 followers in 2017 per VentureBeat, and Wefunder crowdfunding campaigns; no merch or fan accounts found.

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive, memorable product name and a large waitlist for a pre-launch hardware product, but little independent evidence of broad awareness since.

pivots.to: B2B 3D body scanning for gyms, clinics and medspas
pivots.why: Business site and comparison pages target business clients; KingsCrowd reports 375 business clients (company supplied). Timing not sourced precisely.

outcome_analysis: Shape raised money from YC and equity crowdfunding, took $500 preorders in 2017 with a waitlist of about 75,000, and is still active with about 7 staff. Hardware delays and the small funding totals suggest slow progress, but a business customer base and later investor rounds reported by aggregators indicate it survived and found a B2B market; exact reasons are not public.
notes: Company homepage fetch returned only navigation words. The $690K figure is VentureBeat's cumulative equity crowdfunding to date as of May 2017, not a single round; round stage set to other. Wefunder page returned 403 and was not worked around. Aggregators: $4.41M to $4.53M total (The Company Check, CB Insights), Caplight $7.8M with $1M on 2024-05-31 from Alsop Louie Partners, Alumni Ventures and Rebel Fund, Wefunder $216,675 raised at a $40M cap; unverified so not recorded. Competitor sources found (Styku, Fit3D, Naked Labs) are vendor pages from recent years, not dated near 2015, so the list is empty. No outcome news found. Founding year 2015 on YC page; company press release says 2016.
